analysis.title: US Tech Rout / Eurozone GDP & Inflation / Japan Hold & CPI / ECB Moulin & Rehn & Nagel
key_insights: US tech sell-off deepened after Amazon, Intel and Alphabet results, in a market already sensitive to AI capex returns. Last week Meta's capex was seen as too large and Tesla's too small.
Intel beat Q3 expectations but weaker Q4 guidance sent shares more than 20% lower. PC demand is softening while supply constraints limit its ability to meet server demand.
Alphabet's disappointment centred on Search, where faster growth in lower-monetisation AI Mode queries raised questions about core business economics.
Amazon's Q3 AWS growth fell short of elevated expectations, but management gave unusually strong visibility on AWS growth in coming years.
UBS frames the common denominator as disappointments landing in a market highly sensitive to AI investment returns, not a deterioration in AI demand itself.

UBS's US trading team says the tape under Thursday's weak headline index was healthier than it looked, with capital rotating from crowded AI/growth leaders into under-owned cyclicals, value, rate-sensitive exposures (including consumer) and defensives. UBS's Rate Cut Winners basket rose 3.2%.

On Thursday AI Software fell 3.0%, AI Semis 2.9% and AI Risk 2.6%. Retail bought the dip for the sixth time this month, with UBS RMM flow at the 72nd percentile vs 3y. Systematic selling drove excess sell flow.
For Friday, ES1 has the most sell triggers (5 within -2.5%) and RTY1 has the most buy triggers (3 within +2.5%).
Eurozone Q3 GDP rose 0.4% q/q (1.3% y/y) vs UBSe and consensus of 0.2%. Ireland (+5.5% q/q) contributed about 0.2pp, so growth excluding Ireland would be 0.2% q/q.
Within the Eurozone, Spain grew fastest, followed by Germany. Italy and France were stagnant or mildly contracting.

Eurozone inflation: Germany surprised to the downside on food and, less so, services. France rose more than expected on services and energy. Spain eased slightly, in line. UBS tracks Eurozone HICP at about 3.8-3.9% y/y ahead of the 4 November release.
BoJ held at 1.25% on an 8-1 vote. The statement reads modestly hawkish and supports UBS's base case of a December hike. It raised the FY2027 core CPI forecast to 2.6% vs UBS's 2.5%.
BoJ will accelerate ETF disposal to JPY330-860 bn annually from January 2027. Front-end pricing still has three more hikes over the next 12 months.
Tokyo October core CPI rose 2.6% y/y, in line with forecasts and down from 2.7% in September. Excluding fresh food and fuel it slowed to 2.6% from 2.9%.

ECB's Rehn said the energy shock is not over and its pass-through to other prices and wages must be monitored. Moulin said inflation pressures are largely imported. Nagel said policymakers are prepared to raise rates again if needed.
Italy Q3 GDP was flat, in line with UBSe and below the 0.1% consensus.
BoE Decision Maker Panel year-ahead CPI expectations rose to 3.3% from 3.1%. Firms expect year-ahead wage growth of 3.4%.
Australia Q3 final demand PPI ex-exports rose 1.1% q/q vs 1.0% consensus and 1.3% in Q2. Annual inflation held at 3.6%. September headline CPI was 4.3% y/y.
RBNZ's Hansen is '50-50' on a December hike after backing the unexpected OCR hold.
Iran received a letter from VP Vance and signalled no shift in peace terms.
UBS FX Sales notes the USD has been weakening on AI-driven risk-off days, with US yields, DXY and Nasdaq declining together since Nasdaq peaked on Oct. 6.

Nasdaq E-mini futures were down 2% after Amazon and Intel results. Nikkei fell 2.12% and Kospi 3.48%. TY traded 331k overnight, double this week's average, and December hike pricing fell to 18bp from 21bp.
